body.statement: Choose \((h,k)\) by deterministic minimization of \(B(h,k)+S(h,k,\eta)+G(h,k,\eta,\epsilon_n,\delta_n)\) over \(h\le r_0\), \(1\le k\le m h^d\), and \(m h^d\ge C_S^2\log(8/\eta)\). For any deterministic pilot spline dimensions \(J_\pi,J_\mu\ge1\), \(\sup_{Q\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{att}}}\mathbb E_Q[\operatorname{length}\{C_n(h,k)\}]\le C_L r_{\mathrm{up}}\) for a constant \(C_L\) depending only on the fixed class radii, overlap, dimension, and noncoverage level. Thus the expected length is governed, up to fixed logarithmic factors, by the maximum of the KBRW privacy-free term, the \(\gamma\)-smooth private-regression term, and the explicitly derived global-sensitivity higher-order term; no matching full-class lower claim is made.
body.justification: The result gives the first auditable privacy phase diagram for the length, rather than only asymptotic validity of a private causal interval.
body.gap: ShohamEtAl2026 gives a black-box asymptotic resampling interval, and SchroederHartensteinFeuerriegel2025 gives a regular ATE interval; neither derives a pointwise Hölder CATE expected-length phase.
body.consumer: Study designers can select bandwidth, higher-order dimension, and privacy budget to meet a prespecified interval-width requirement.
